messages:
Maya: Heads-up — after the dedicated rollout last night we had a short overload event at ~03:14 UTC. Spike from ~100 rps to ~1.6k rps for ~45s, several 503s. Anyone tracing how burst was handled at the edge?

Dave: I saw it in the traces. Most requests hit the ingress tier and we dropped when internal leaky-shaper queue filled. Token-bucket counters on the org side stayed mostly fine.

Lina: Yup, infra logs show the ingress leaky-bucket leak_rate was defaulted to 250 rps and capacity 400 — too small for the pattern. The spike was short but huge.

Maya: Question: do we want to tune ingress leaky bucket bigger, or rely on per-org token buckets with higher refill?

Dave: Quick thought: leaky-bucket at edge smooths short spikes -> protects runtime and keeps latency stable. Token-bucket per-org is for steady-state quotas and controlled bursts. We should use both.

Jason: UX angle — customers expect short bursts for interactive apps. Console needs an explicit "burst window" and preview of the effective RPS over that window. Right now it's opaque.

Lina: Agree on both. Proposed defaults: make ingress leaky_bucket leak_rate = 300 rps, capacity = 1200 (handles ~4s of full 1200rps -> smooth), and keep org token_bucket refill_rate = configurable per plan.

Maya: Can we show example config quickly so SREs/ops can test?

Dave: Sure — example we used in staging:

```yaml
ingress_shaper:
  type: leaky_bucket
  leak_rate_rps: 300
  capacity_tokens: 1200

org_quota:
  type: token_bucket
  refill_rate_rps: 50
  capacity_tokens: 2000
```

Dave: Notes: capacity_tokens ~= max instantaneous requests we allow to queue/smooth. leak_rate controls sustained outflow. Token bucket refill_rate is per-org long-window throughput.

Lina: Also want to record metrics so we can tune: ingress.leaky.queue_size, ingress.leaky.drops, org.bucket.tokens_used, org.bucket.refill_rate_effective. Add a burst_consumption histogram with short windows (1s,5s,30s).

Maya: +1 on metrics. We were blind last night for ~30s. If we had a 5s burst chart we would have noticed early.

Jason: UX: expose two knobs in console: "short-burst allowance (seconds)" and "burst ceiling (tokens)" with tooltips linking to perf guidance. Also surface 'predicted 99th latency increase' when you change settings.

Dave: Implementation plan idea: 1) quick staging change to ingress defaults, 2) roll to a subset (canary) with ingress-metrics dashboard, 3) if stable, rollout org token-bucket policy changes and console update.

Lina: Canary suggestions: 1% of orgs, pick a noisy org we know (not prod-critical). Add alert rule: ingress.leaky.drops > 5 in 1m -> rollback canary.

Maya: Sounds good. Action items: @Dave update staging config + create dashboard; @Lina add alerts and metrics; @Jason draft console UX copy. I'll coordinate canary cohort.

infra-bot: deploy triggered by Dave to staging at 2026-03-18T06:10:00Z :arrow_up:  (job id 88921)

Dave: Started deploying staging change now. I'll post results and a couple of latency/burst charts in here once we have ~30m of data.

Maya: Thanks — appreciate quick turnaround. If we still see 5xxs after smoothing we'll consider rejecting heavier bursts at ingress with a clear 429 + Retry-After header and console explanation. :thumbsup:

Lina: One more operational note: make sure we don't silently convert 503s -> 200s with queued long tails. Keep p99 latency SLO checks in place.

Maya: Agreed. Decision for now (informal): ingress leaky-bucket smoothing enabled with leak_rate 300 rps, capacity 1200; keep per-org token-bucket for quota. Console changes + metrics+alerts as above. We'll revisit after canary.

(emoji reactions: Maya :eyes:, Dave :rocket:, Lina :white_check_mark:, Jason :memo:)
